proposals.name: Early CSM dust obscuration
proposals.idea: The transient is an interacting supernova whose intrinsic plateau evolves slowly, but dust rapidly condenses in the cold dense post-shock circumstellar shell beginning near optical peak. The growing wavelength-dependent extinction preferentially suppresses the g band, producing the unexpectedly fast blue fading without requiring equally fast intrinsic fading.

equation.flux: host_b + step(age - 0.01) * amp_b * rise * fade * exp(-dust_b * dust_on)

t0.meaning: explosion time in days relative to now

t_dust.meaning: midpoint time of rapid dust formation

w_dust.meaning: duration of the dust-formation transition in days

amp_b.meaning: unextincted peak flux scale per band in microjansky

dust_b.meaning: final dust optical depth per band, expected larger in g than r

host_b.meaning: constant host or background flux per band in microjansky

proposals.predicts: It predicts the g-band decline will flatten to a dust-attenuated level after condensation completes, accompanied by a smaller delayed r-band step and saturation at a red g-r color, rather than the smooth parallel color evolution of the failed supernova hypotheses.

proposals.name: Cooling Wien-tail fireball
proposals.idea: An expanding ejecta photosphere cools as a power law in time with no sustained radioactive or plateau heating, so its radius growth first raises the flux and then the falling temperature drives each band onto the exponential Wien tail. The bluer g band is suppressed earlier and faster than r, producing the observed rapid reddening and accelerated g-band fade that standard supernova templates miss.

t0.meaning: explosion time in days relative to now

tau_rise.meaning: photospheric expansion rise timescale in days

amp_b.meaning: per-band flux scale in microjansky before Wien suppression

wien_b.meaning: per-band Wien-tail coefficient, larger for g than r

proposals.predicts: The r band will soon follow g into an accelerating exponential decline with monotonically reddening g-r color and no supernova plateau or cobalt-powered tail flattening.

proposals.name: luminous red nova merger
proposals.idea: A stellar merger ejecting a common envelope produces an expanding, cooling photosphere with no radioactive reheating to sustain the blue light. As the temperature falls, g-band emission on the Wien tail collapses rapidly while r-band emission is sustained much longer by the cool, large photosphere.

t_exp.meaning: merger and envelope ejection time in days

tau_rise.meaning: rise time of the expanding envelope in days

area_pow.meaning: power-law growth of photospheric emitting area

cool_pow.meaning: power-law index for photospheric cooling with age

tail_pow.meaning: power-law decay index of the cool red tail

hot_b.meaning: hot photosphere flux per band at age 10 days in microjansky

sens_b.meaning: per-band Wien-tail sensitivity to cooling, larger in g than r

cool_b.meaning: cool red-tail flux per band at age 10 days in microjansky

proposals.predicts: It predicts g continues fading steeply with g-r reddening beyond about 1.5 mag while r follows a slow power-law plateau for weeks, with no supernova-like rebrightening or abrupt plateau end.
